transcript:
User: We have a girl at the front desk, she picks up fine. Not sure why I'd need this.
Agent: Got it, if she’s handling calls well it makes sense you’d question it.  

Mhm, when she’s at lunch, on another call, or out for the day, what typically happens to incoming calls?
User: Well, we just call people back when we can. We haven't really counted any missed calls.
Agent: Makes sense, a lot of offices work that way.  

When you do call folks back, do you ever hear “oh, I already booked somewhere else” or “I’m at work now, can’t talk”?
User: Sure, sometimes that happens, but it's not like it's a huge issue for us.
Agent: Yeah, that’s fair — if it’s not a big issue, there’s no reason to overhaul anything.  

Just so I don’t waste your time, are you more focused on keeping the phones covered perfectly, or on getting more new customers in the door?
User: Keeping the phones covered is important, but we've been managing. New customers are always good, though.
Agent: Totally hear you — sounds like things are “fine,” and you’re open if it adds more new customers.  

So if nothing broke, but you could turn a few of those “we’ll call you back” folks into booked appointments automatically, would that actually matter to you, or would it be more of a nice-to-have?
User: If it genuinely brings in more business without disrupting Janet, it might be worth considering as a backup.
Agent: Totally makes sense — as a backup that quietly brings in more business while Janet keeps doing her thing.  

When Janet can’t grab the phone — lunch, busy with a customer, out sick — would you want those calls to turn into booked appointments automatically, or even just clean voicemails with all the info you need?
User: Alright, as a backup layer, I can see it being useful. Let's book that demo to explore.
Agent: Gotcha, so you’re open to it as a backup that helps capture more business.  

What’s usually better for you for a quick demo with Jay — earlier in the day or later afternoon?
User: Earlier in the day works best for me. Let's get that demo scheduled.
Agent: Got it, earlier is better for you.  

What day over the next few days is easiest for a 20‑minute call with Jay — tomorrow, the following day, or later in the week?
User: Tomorrow morning works for me. Let's go ahead and schedule it then.
Agent: Nice, tomorrow morning it is.  

Are you generally more free around 9, 10, or 11 your time for that 20‑minute call with Jay, no commitment—see it in action, then decide?
User: Let's go with 10 AM. That should work for me.
Agent: Perfect, we’ll lock in tomorrow at 10 AM for a 20‑minute call with Jay, no commitment—just see it in action and then you can decide.  

What’s your first name and the best email, so Jay can send over the calendar invite and meeting link?
User: Dave. Send the invite to dave@kowalskiautobody.com. Looking forward to seeing how this can fit in.
Agent: Thanks, Dave — I’ve got you down for tomorrow at 10 AM with Jay, and we’ll send the calendar invite to dave@kowalskiautobody.com shortly. You’ll see exactly how the backup layer works without getting in Janet’s way, and you can decide from there if it’s worth it for your shop; if anything comes up before then, just reply to the invite to reschedule. Thanks again for taking the time today, talk to you tomorrow!
